draft.title: Motion timing thresholds + easing derivation
draft.principle_summary: Interactive timing is governed by three converging, independently-sourced perceptual bands (Doherty and Thadani's 1982 IBM finding that throughput rises sharply once system response drops under about 400ms; Miller 1968 and Nielsen 1993's coarser 0.1s / 1s / 10s attention bands; and the modern operational form, Google's RAIL model, response <=100ms feels instant, animation frames <=16ms hold 60fps, load feedback matters up to about 1000ms, with Core Web Vitals INP codifying <=200ms at p75 as the current "good" bar). These bands do not compete, they nest: RAIL's 100ms response ceiling sits inside Doherty's 400ms throughput ceiling, which sits inside Miller/Nielsen's 1s flow ceiling. Easing curve choice is a second, separate axis: Material Design's four canonical curves (standard cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) for in-place moves, decelerate for entrances, accelerate for exits, sharp for temporary exits) encode the physical read of a motion (arriving vs leaving vs continuing), not a timing threshold. A duration inside the right band with the wrong curve semantics still reads as wrong.

sources.claim: Doherty and Thadani (IBM Systems Journal, 1982) found user throughput/productivity rises sharply once system response time drops below roughly 400ms; the informal '400ms makes computing addictive' framing is a later dramatization of the same finding.
sources.source: Doherty, W.J. and Thadani, A.J., 'The Economic Value of Rapid Response Time', IBM Systems Journal, 1982; summarized at Laws of UX (lawsofux.com/doherty-threshold) and daverupert.com/2015/06/doherty-threshold

sources.claim: Miller (1968) and Nielsen (1993) establish three response-time bands: about 0.1s feels instantaneous, about 1s keeps the user's flow of thought uninterrupted, about 10s is the limit of attention before the user disengages.
sources.source: Miller, R.B., 'Response time in man-computer conversational transactions', 1968; Nielsen, J., 'Response Times: The 3 Important Limits', Nielsen Norman Group, 1993 (nngroup.com/articles/response-times-3-important-limits)

sources.claim: Google's RAIL performance model sets three of the same-family thresholds in operational form: input response should complete within 100ms to feel instant, each animation frame has a 16ms budget to sustain 60fps, and load/idle work has roughly a 1000ms budget before users lose the sense that something is happening.
sources.source: web.dev, 'Measure Performance with the RAIL Model' (web.dev/articles/rail), Google Chrome team

sources.claim: Core Web Vitals' Interaction to Next Paint (INP) sets <=200ms at the 75th percentile as the current 'good' threshold for perceived responsiveness, the modern operational descendant of the Doherty/RAIL response bands.
sources.source: web.dev, 'Interaction to Next Paint (INP)' (web.dev/articles/inp), Google Chrome team, Core Web Vitals

sources.claim: Material Design's motion system specifies four semantic easing curves: standard (in-place moves), decelerate (entrances, fast start then settle), accelerate (permanent exits, speeds off), and sharp (temporary exits that may return). The standard curve's canonical bezier is cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0), which is the exact curve Solen's locked 'snap' token uses.
sources.source: Material Design (Material 1 archive), 'Duration & easing' (m1.material.io/motion/duration-easing.html) and Material Design 3, 'Easing and duration' (m3.material.io/styles/motion/easing-and-duration)

sources.claim: Material Design's own duration guidance bands by platform and scale: mobile animations generally 200-300ms (larger moves 300-400ms, smaller ones 150-200ms), desktop animations generally 150-200ms, duration scaling down roughly 30% on smaller-screen wearables.

A near-threshold, single-channel motion cue (opacity fade alone, no accompanying position/scale/blur change) can fall below a viewer's just-noticeable-difference for that cue and read as no motion at all; combining multiple simultaneous channels (position + scale + blur, as Solen's 420ms entrance recipe does) crosses the noticeability threshold more reliably than any one channel alone. This is a general perceptual-detection principle (Weber-Fechner just-noticeable-difference), not a study of this exact UI case.
sources.source: Weber-Fechner law of just-noticeable difference (general psychophysics, foundational, no single modern citation needed as a named study); applied here only as the mechanism explanation for Solen's own logged owner finding

draft.solen_current: _design-system/RATIONALE.md section 7 (lines 161-173, "Domain 6: Motion and timing") already carries partial grounding: it correctly cites Miller 1968 / Nielsen 1993 for the 0.1s/1s/10s bands, correctly de-dramatizes Doherty and Thadani 1982 into "throughput rises sharply under ~400ms" (folklore table line 245 explicitly bans the "addictive" framing), cites INP <=200ms at p75 as the modern operational form, and audits the locked 80/150/200/250/300/500ms whitelist (LOCKFILE:575) plus the 420ms entrance recipe against that band, correctly flagging 420ms as a documented departure rather than silently citing NN/g while shipping something outside it. Easing semantics (line 167) are labeled T2 Material-motion-research and correctly map snap/spring/glide/thud to standard/overshoot/decelerate/accelerate. RATIONALE.md:171 also correctly wires prefers-reduced-motion to WCAG 2.3.3 (T1) and flags it as under-documented outside globals.css. MOTION.md:42-43 records the negative empirical datum (opacity-only fade reverted as imperceptible to the owner) and correctly reasons "opacity alone is invisible; scale alone reads as [incomplete elsewhere]", motivating the multi-property "blur is non-negotiable" rule.
draft.gap: Two gaps, both narrow since the section is already partial not bare. First, RAIL is never named even though it is the standard modern operational form that Solen's own INP citation descends from: the file cites INP but skips the 16ms-frame / 100ms-response / 1000ms-load ladder that would let a reader see WHY 100ms is the response ceiling and not, say, 150ms, and would let the 80ms/150ms members of the duration whitelist trace to a named source (RAIL's 100ms response ceiling) rather than only to NN/g's looser "micro-feedback ~100ms" prose. Second, the easing-curve line (167) says "Material motion research" without ever stating the actual Material curve math, so a reader cannot verify that Solen's "snap" token (cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)) is not just Material-flavored but is LITERALLY Material's canonical standard curve value, the strongest, most checkable form the claim could take. Third, the negative empirical datum in MOTION.md (opacity-only fade found imperceptible) is recorded as an observation but never given a mechanism: RATIONALE.md section 7 states the fact of the departure (420ms, multi-property) but does not connect it to why a single weak channel can fall below a noticeability floor while several channels together do not, leaving future readers to re-derive or re-guess the reasoning MOTION.md already paid for empirically.
draft.proposed_addition:
Insert as a new paragraph immediately after the existing "Response thresholds (T1-T2)" paragraph in RATIONALE.md section 7 (after line 163), before the "Solen ladder audit" paragraph. Format matches the section's existing prose-paragraph convention (this section does not use the DECISION/FORCES block format used in section 14's retrofit blocks, so the addition below follows section 7's own established style rather than importing a block format that would look inconsistent next to its neighbors).

DECISION: Cite RAIL by name alongside Miller/Nielsen and Doherty as the third, nested band that INP descends from, and state the Material standard-curve bezier explicitly so the snap token's match is checkable rather than asserted.

FORCES: naming a fourth framework (RAIL) against the two already cited (Miller/Nielsen, Doherty) risks looking like citation-padding versus the real payoff, that RAIL is the direct ancestor of the INP number already in the doc and explains WHY 100ms and not another value; stating the exact Material bezier risks the doc looking like it is "deriving" a locked literal versus what it is actually doing, showing that a value already locked in LOCKFILE happens to equal a named external standard, which is retrofit not re-derivation.

OPTIMIZES FOR: every number in the duration whitelist becoming traceable to a specific named external band (RAIL's 16/100/1000ms triad, Doherty's ~400ms ceiling, Miller/Nielsen's 0.1/1/10s bands) instead of only NN/g's looser prose guidance; the easing semantics line becoming independently checkable (a reader can go compute cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) and see it matches Material's own standard-curve documentation) instead of resting on "Material motion research" as an unverifiable gesture.

SACRIFICES: nothing structural, this is additive grounding under an already-partial section; the only cost is a few more lines and a few more citations to keep current if any of the source pages move.

BOUNDARY: this does not reopen or re-derive the LOCKFILE duration whitelist (80/150/200/250/300/500ms) or the four easing tokens (snap/spring/glide/thud), and it does not touch the documented 420ms entrance departure, which stays recorded as a deliberate owner-approved departure, not something this addition tries to re-justify into the standard band. It also does not resolve the "spring exists twice with different math" open inconsistency flagged at RATIONALE.md:169, that stays a separate flagged item.

MECHANIC (T1-T2, RAIL, web.dev): RAIL names four life-cycle phases, Response, Animation, Idle, Load. Its two thresholds relevant to Solen's duration ladder: input response should complete within 100ms to read as instant (the direct ancestor of the INP <=200ms "good" p75 bar already cited), and each animation frame has a 16ms budget to sustain 60fps (the frame-rate floor underneath every CSS transition in the app, independent of which duration token is chosen). RAIL's third relevant number, roughly 1000ms as the ceiling before users lose the sense that "something is happening" during load, nests inside Miller/Nielsen's already-cited 1s flow-keeping band rather than adding a new one, it is the same finding restated in modern web-performance vocabulary.

MECHANIC (CONV, Material Design, checkable): Material's four semantic easing curves are standard (in-place moves, cubic-bezier(0.4,0.0,0.2,1.0)), decelerate (entrances), accelerate (permanent exits), and sharp (temporary exits that may return). Solen's "snap" token is not merely "Material-flavored", its bezier values are numerically identical to Material's own standard-curve constant. This upgrades the existing "semantics were chosen right" line from a T2 research-alignment claim to a directly checkable literal match, while spring/glide/thud remain Solen-tuned variants that follow Material's SEMANTIC pattern (overshoot-for-reveal, decelerate-for-entrance, accelerate-for-exit) without matching Material's exact bezier constants for those three, which is the honest distinction to keep.

MECHANIC (T3, Weber-Fechner just-noticeable-difference, applied): MOTION.md's logged finding, an opacity-only fade was imperceptible to the owner and reverted, is best read through the general psychophysics principle that any single perceptual channel needs to cross its own just-noticeable-difference floor to register, and a slow, low-magnitude opacity ramp with no accompanying edge, position, or focus change can sit below that floor even though it is objectively happening. Combining channels (Solen's 420ms entrance recipe layers position, scale, and blur) does not lower any one channel's JND, it gives the visual system multiple simultaneous cues, any one of which crossing threshold makes the whole change register as motion. This is offered as a T3 explanatory mechanism for an already-logged empirical result, not a new empirical claim, and should be labeled as such rather than upgraded to T1 in the doc.

Taste Lab probe (only if the owner wants to calibrate further, not required to close this gap): a staircase probe varying ONE channel at a time (opacity alone, position alone, scale alone, blur alone) at a fixed 300-400ms duration on a real Solen card entrance, asking only "did you see it move, yes or no" at each step, would locate each channel's individual JND on the actual product surface and let a future revision state a number instead of only the mechanism. This is exactly the kind of continuous-axis calibration the epistemic-stance section (RATIONALE.md:689) already flags as the right use of staircase/adaptive probes, cross-reference rather than duplicate that method description.
numbers_used: cubic-bezier(0.4,0.0,0.2,1.0) (Material standard curve, matches Solen 'snap' token)
80/150/200/250/300/500ms (Solen locked duration whitelist, LOCKFILE:575, cited not changed)
420ms (Solen locked entrance recipe, MOTION.md:28, cited not changed)

Feeds directly into the epistemic-stance section's existing staircase/adaptive-probe method (RATIONALE.md:689), cross-reference rather than duplicate.

claim_verdicts.claim: Doherty and Thadani (IBM Systems Journal, 1982) found throughput rises sharply once response time drops below ~400ms; the 'addictive' framing is a later dramatization.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed real 1982 IBM Systems Journal paper, title and 400ms threshold match (Laws of UX, daverupert.com summaries agree). One nuance: secondary sources describe the 'addicting' language as tied closely to the original 1982 usage itself, not purely a later add-on, so 'later dramatization' slightly understates how early that framing appeared. Does not change the claim's validity or the correct decision to keep 'addictive' out of Solen's own doc (already banned per the draft's own note).

claim_verdicts.claim: Miller (1968) and Nielsen (1993) establish 0.1s / 1s / 10s response-time bands.
claim_verdicts.note: NN/g 'Response Times: The 3 Important Limits' (Nielsen 1993, building on Miller 1968) is a stable, well-established, primary-adjacent HCI source. Tier T1 held.

claim_verdicts.claim: RAIL model: 100ms response ceiling, 16ms animation frame budget, ~1000ms load/idle ceiling.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed via web.dev-derived secondary sources: Response <=100ms (visible within 100ms), Animation 16ms/frame budget for 60fps, Load target ~1000ms to feel interactive. Numbers match the draft. One of the search sources conflated the RAIL 'Load' target with a looser '5 seconds on mid-range devices' framing found elsewhere; the draft correctly uses the tighter 1000ms figure that matches RAIL's own named phase target, not the looser mobile-network caveat some blogs add.

claim_verdicts.claim: Core Web Vitals INP <=200ms at p75 is the current 'good' threshold.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed directly: web.dev and multiple current (2026) sources state INP good = <=200ms at 75th percentile field data, 200-500ms needs improvement, >500ms poor. Number and percentile both match the draft exactly.

claim_verdicts.claim: Material Design's four semantic easing curves (standard/decelerate/accelerate/sharp); standard = cubic-bezier(0.4,0.0,0.2,1.0), matching Solen's 'snap' token.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) is Material's documented standard curve and is widely cited as such. The four-curve semantic split (standard/decelerate/accelerate/sharp) is also standard Material 1 documentation. Whether Solen's 'snap' token is numerically identical was not independently re-verified against Solen's own token file in this pass (that check belongs to the codebase, not an external source check) -- flagged in residual_risks, not a source failure.

claim_verdicts.claim: Material duration guidance: mobile 200-300ms (larger 300-400ms, smaller 150-200ms), desktop 150-200ms.
claim_verdicts.note: Could not independently confirm this exact mobile/desktop duration split against m1.material.io in this pass; the web search surfaced a different generic figure ('UI transitions 150-300ms, emphasis motions 400-600ms', sourced closer to Carbon Design System framing, not confirmed as Material's own archive numbers). Downgraded from CONV to T3 (unverified specificity) as a caution. Low impact: these specific duration-split numbers appear only in the draft's sources[]/numbers_used[] lists and are NOT quoted inside the actual proposed_addition text inserted into RATIONALE.md, so this softening does not require editing the addition itself.

claim_verdicts.claim: Weber-Fechner just-noticeable-difference as the mechanism for why an opacity-only fade read as imperceptible while multi-channel (position+scale+blur) motion registered.
claim_verdicts.note: Weber-Fechner is a real, foundational psychophysics principle; correctly applied here as an explanatory mechanism for an already-logged empirical Solen finding (MOTION.md opacity-fade revert), not as a new empirical claim about this UI. Tier T3 (general-principle-applied, not a study of this exact case) is the honest and correctly assigned tier, matches the draft's own labeling.
